brief:
# Build: whats-new-banner (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now.

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `whats-new-banner`, branch claude/whats-new-banner) with the steps below + in-progress banner entry, per standing rules. Check the pending queue.
- Running in parallel: `orch-live-sync` (live store writes to main, reconciler, banners/THREADS follow the store, per-step branch/pr/merged fields), `notes-vault`, `headless-tabs`. Never hand-edit store.json; use the orchestrator CLI. Reuse orch-live-sync's events (framework/cli/builds-live.mjs, reconciler) if they are on main when you need them; otherwise read the store + GitHub merged PRs directly and leave a seam to switch over.

## What Brett wants
A **What's new** banner that shows new features that have been pushed out (merged to main and deployed), filterable/groupable **by date, by build, and by app** (all three).

## Steps
- s1 Feed: a `whats-new@1` feed built from what actually shipped: builds/steps whose code merged to main (store merged/mergedAt, merged PRs, build reports' Added/Changed sections, Codebase Changes plugin entries). Each item: title (plain-language feature, from the build report/PR, not commit-speak), build id, profile, apps affected (from changed paths: apps/console-web, axhub-web, amberx-droid, molly, plugins/<x> -> app/plugin names), date merged, deployed yes/no (deploy workflow run for that commit), links (PR, report). Server route + cached file; updates when the store/merges change (no model tokens).
- s2 Banner: a `whats-new` banner asset/widget (banner-pack conventions, works in the banner editor and gallery): compact ticker of the newest shipped features with an unread count; tap opens a panel.
- s3 Panel: list grouped by Date (Today / Yesterday / this week / older), By build, or By app (segmented switch, remembered); search; per-item details (what it does, where to find it, PR/report links); mark read / mark all read; 'new since last visit' highlighting.
- s4 Settings: show/hide the banner, which apps to include, how far back, only deployed vs merged.
- s5 Help pack, tests, check-theme/check-controls, lifecycle, UI Review shots (phone + desktop), report `_claude/builds/reports/whats-new-banner.md`, THREADS.md, PR. Mark each step done through the store as you finish it.
Tokens only, follows the hub look. Android: deferred gap in PORTING.md. Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - three states
The feed and panel show three sections/states, each still groupable by date, build and app:
1. **Live** - merged to main AND deployed.
2. **Merged** - on main, not deployed yet.
3. **Ready to merge** - built and finished but not merged: open PRs for builds/steps marked done, plus finished headless builds whose branch is ahead of main with no PR (vps build_list 'finished, not landed'). For each item show what it's waiting on in plain words: UI Review approval (with the review group name and a button that opens it), CI red/pending, waiting on another PR first (merge order, e.g. #245 before #252), sync hold, or nothing (ready now). Link to the PR.
Banner ticker shows counts per state (e.g. '3 live, 2 merged, 10 waiting'). Reuse the push banner's PR data if it already has it instead of fetching twice; don't duplicate its merge actions (link to it).

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - Go-to hook
- Tapping/clicking an item does NOT navigate; it only expands its details.
- Every **Live** item carries its own hook: a small 'Go to it' button/icon on the item. Clicking the hook takes you to the feature itself: opens the right app/plugin/window/tab, scrolls to and briefly highlights the exact control or setting (e.g. Terminal > Settings > Tooltip mode), using axf:// deep links / the router + the element's control id / help id. Each feed item stores its target (deep link + control id) in whats-new@1, filled from the build report / changed controls; if a target can't be resolved, the hook opens the closest screen and says so.
- Merged (not deployed) and Ready-to-merge items get no Go-to hook (feature isn't live); they keep their PR / UI Review links.
- Tests for target resolution + highlight; shots of the hook and the highlight.
